messages:
sam: heads up — noticed a p99 jump on Mixtral-6B-MoE after the kernel bump (deploy @ 1723450000). p50 stable, but p95/p99 doubled. :thinking_face:
ani: ugh. any reproducible load? internal canary or perf harness? :eyes:
sam: repro in perf harness and small canary. quick numbers: p99 went from ~48ms -> ~92ms under our standard 64-concurrency test. throughput drop ~18%. GPU util dropped ~6% while CPU spikes on router threads.
oliver: sharing profiler traces now. looks like a kernel fallback path is triggering for attention+softmax when head_dim % 8 != 0 after the kernel change. that causes an unfused path hitting host kernels for softmax+scale.
jia: interesting — that would explain CPU work on router threads. do we have kv cache metrics? cache hit ratio drop?
sam: yes. kv_cache_hit_rate per-request fell from 87% -> 62% for topk=2 routing, per our telemetry. eviction rate up ~3x.
rafa: that smells like routing churn: more requests hitting different experts, invalidating prefix-aligned kv entries. could be router logits being noisier after the model update or numerical change in kernel.
ani: can someone paste the kernel perf snippet?
oliver: pasted below — nvprof-style tail + flame summary.
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                             Calls  Avg(ms)
0.85      mix_attn_fused_fp16                 1200   0.0007
2.30      aten::softmax_fp32_fallback         450    0.0051  <-- increased
1.10      moe_router_forward                  1800   0.0006
3.50      kv_cache_lookup_host                900    0.0039
```

oliver: note the aten::softmax_fp32_fallback spikes vs baseline where we had a fused softmax path.
sam: config: Mixtral-6B-MoE, topk=2, router_temp=1.0, expert_parallelism=1 (one expert shard per replica), dynamic_batch.window_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=4096.
jia: two immediate experiment ideas: 1) change router_temp down to 0.8 to reduce routing jitter; 2) bump topk from 2->3 or 4 to reduce reroutes (but increases compute). anyone want to try quick canary?
ani: also try a quick kernel rollback to pre-bump fused-kernel (build id 2026-02-18) to confirm causality.
rafa: on the KV side, we should consider increasing kv_cache_capacity per expert or switching to LRU windowing to tolerate small routing churn spikes. but that increases memory footprint. tradeoffs.
sam: I ran kernel-rollback on a tiny canary: p99 dropped back to ~50ms, kv hits recovered to ~84%. so likely the new kernel path introduced the numerical layout that prevents fused softmax.
oli ver: (typo) oliver: thanks for rollback test — confirms. we need a fix: either patch kernel to support head dims mod 8 or add a fast path guard that uses the fused kernel for Mixtral head dims by padding to 64 when launching kernel (cheap) or fallback to blocking fused call.
jia: padding head dim at runtime might be simplest short-term: pad sequence dims for the fused kernel launch and trim output. low risk but must check memory and perf.
ani: while we triage kernel fix, we should mitigate at router level: increase router_temp=0.85 and topk=3 for critical tenants. Also enable adaptive_cache_ttl so kv entries live longer for experts that have >10% churn.
sam: i've queued a canary with router_temp=0.85 + topk=3 + kernel-rollback off (so we can see if router knobs help). job id: perf/1723456791.
perf-ci-bot: perf run started: perf/1723456791. baseline: mixtral-6b-mo e standard harness. ETA ~20m.
rafa: also a reminder: expert_parallelism=1 means each replica owns all experts it serves. if we increase parallelism (replicate experts across devices) we can reduce cross-replica router hops, but that raises memory and reduces max_model_instances per GPU. not free.
oliver: did a micro-sim that shows increasing expert_parallelism to 2 reduces router network traffic by ~22% and increases kv hit by ~9% in sim, but raw compute goes up ~12%.
jia: can we do selective replication? replicate hot experts only. we have hotset metric per-expert. replicate top 10% hot experts as a pilot.
sam: agree. can we implement a small scheduler change: hot-expert-replicate thresh=0.10, replicate_count=2, eviction_penalty=1.2? that should be a cheap config change in router.
ani: also open question: batching heuristics. the kernel bump changed fusing which made small batches relatively more expensive. we might want to adjust dynamic_batch.window_ms down to 8ms to favor latency on critical routes, or up to 16ms to amortize fixed kernel cost (depends on SLO). we need to run both.
rafa: take care: increasing batch window can amplify cache thrash since larger batches interleave more prefixes. but it's workload dependent.
sam: plan of action summarized: 1) rollback kernel in canary (done), 2) run router knobs experiment (temp=0.85, topk=3), 3) run selective-replication pilot for hot experts, 4) perf regress root cause with kernel team for fused softmax alignment. I'll post results.
deploy-bot: canary perf/1723456791 finished: p99=56ms, kv_hit=81%, throughput -4% vs baseline.
ania: results look promising. p99 not fully restored but improved. next: try selective-replication + kernel patch in staging.
oliver: i'll file a kernel bug with repro, attaching a minimal repro harness and trace. cc @kernel-team.
raf a: one more datapoint — when I forced topk=4 in perf harness (no kernel rollback) p99 returned to ~60ms but GPU utilization jumped and total tokens/sec dropped ~11%. tradeoff clear.
jia: thumbs — let's proceed with router temp + topk=3 for prod mitigation, schedule kernel fix priority P1, and plan selective replication pilot next week.
sam: assigning follow-ups: @oliver file kernel bug & repro, @rafa prototype selective replication scheduler change, @jia run batch window sensitivity sweeps (8/12/16ms) and post matrix. i'll coordinate canaries.
perf-ci-bot: note: saved perf artifacts at https://perf.internal.redwood/1723456791/artifacts : flame, traces, kv-metrics.csv
sam: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for updates. :rocket:
